summary: Full first-pass test of OAKsphere Connect (backend + frontend). Backend: 66 pytest cases across auth, leads CRUD/filters/saved-views/CSV, role scoping, assignment (manual+auto), calling list, ALL 4 call-disposition validation rules, follow-up engine, interviews, joinings, dashboards (main/funnel/targets/leaderboard/action-required/my-day/scorecard), clients, jobs, users, settings, notifications, audit — 66/66 passed. Frontend: Playwright flows for admin, team-leader and recruiter roles. Core loop works end-to-end (login -> dashboard KPIs/funnel/leaderboard/comparison, leads table with priority + '⚠ VERIFY' flag, 7 saved-view chips, priority filter, global search, lead drawer with timeline, Add Lead + duplicate warning, bulk assign, auto-distribute, CSV download, prioritized calling queue with 'Overdue Follow-up' first, disposition validations all enforced with error toasts, follow-up tabs + Done, interview stage/confirmation persistence, joining status persistence, jobs/clients add, recruiters add/toggle/reset-pw, all 5 report tabs, 8 Action-Required sections, settings persistence, My Day 6-step stepper). Main defect class found: MISSING ROLE GUARDS on frontend routes + unscoped admin data in 3 backend endpoints, plus missing error handling on several mutations.

critical.issue: No role restriction (uses get_current_user). A recruiter receives the FULL roster of every recruiter/team-leader incl. emails, phones and per-user performance stats. Violates 'Recruiter = only assigned leads' rule.

Only lead-based sections are scoped. unconfirmed_tomorrow_interviews (db.interviews.find({})), unconfirmed_joinings (db.joinings.find(...)) and recruiters_below_target (all active recruiters + their call counts) ignore scope_recruiter_ids, so a recruiter sees other recruiters' candidates and call performance. Verified: recruiter Harshika got 2 unconfirmed joinings, 3 tomorrow interviews and call stats for all 4 recruiters.
Unscoped for every role (recruiter sees all recruiters' scores). Intentional for gamification? If so ignore, otherwise scope it.

minor.issue: Falls back to hardcoded 'recruiter123'; frontend always sends that literal for ANY user including team_leader. During testing this silently changed the seeded Team Leader password (teamlead123 -> recruiter123) and broke TL login. Password was restored by the test agent.
Duplicate detection compares the raw phone string only. '+91 900000 1000' vs '919000001000' vs '9000001000' are NOT flagged as duplicates. Normalise to digits (last 10) before matching.
Body accepted as raw dict (no Pydantic model) on many write endpoints — arbitrary keys are persisted into the documents.
N+1 query pattern: enrich_lead/enrich_interview/enrich_joining issue one or more DB round trips per row (interviews do 4 per row). Fine for demo volume, will not scale.

ui_bugs.issue: No role-based route guards. Logged-in recruiter can open /recruiters (full roster page), /settings (admin config editor), /action-required and /import by typing the URL — sidebar hides the links but the pages render with real admin data.

No try/catch on the save call: a recruiter clicking Save changes gets an unhandled rejection (console/pageerror 'Request failed with status code 403') and NO error toast — screen looks unchanged with no feedback.
Unread badge is only refetched on route change (useEffect [pathname]). After 'Mark all read' the bell still shows the old count (2) until navigation. 'Mark all read' also shows no success toast.
Reset Password fires immediately with hardcoded 'recruiter123' — no confirm dialog, no custom-password input, no error handling; toast prints the password in plain text.
checkDup runs only onBlur of the phone field, so a user who types a duplicate number and clicks Save directly never sees the warning (works when the field loses focus).
doAssign, autoDistribute, exportCsv, toggleActive have no .catch — any API failure is a silent no-op (only success toasts exist).

Recruiter demo testid is 'demo-login-recruiter-harshika-' (trailing dash from the slug regex) — differs from the documented id; also these buttons only pre-fill the form, they do not log in (label says 'tap to fill', acceptable but note the testid).

integration_issues.issue: Assign dropdown lists the Team Leader as an assignable 'recruiter' (from /api/recruiters). Leads can therefore be assigned to a team leader — confirm this is intended.
One run produced no toast after changing confirmation (stage change did toast); value did persist on reload and PATCH is verified green in pytest — likely toast dedup, low confidence, worth a glance.

design_issues.screen: Dashboard KPI cards / Recruiters cards / Reports
issues: Labels and emails use text-slate-400 on white (e.g. 'CONNECTED', 'LEADS', recruiter email) — ~2.6:1 contrast, fails WCAG AA for small text
KPI cards have large empty right-hand space at 1920px
'Original time' rendered as raw locale string '4/9/2026, 2:48:32 am' while the rest of the app uses '04 Sept, 02:48 pm' — inconsistent date formatting
'All Leads' and 'My Leads' are both shown to recruiters and return identical data (scope = self), redundant navigation

action_items: Add role guards to frontend routes (/recruiters, /settings, /action-required, /import → admin/team_leader only) and redirect unauthorised roles
Restrict GET /api/recruiters to admin/team_leader (or return only self for recruiters)
Scope unconfirmed_tomorrow_interviews, unconfirmed_joinings and recruiters_below_target in /api/dashboard/action-required by scope_recruiter_ids
Add try/catch + error toast to Settings save, Leads assign/auto-distribute/export, Recruiters toggle/resetPw
Refresh unread notification count after 'Mark all read' (and add a success toast)
Reset Password: add confirm dialog + allow a custom password; never apply the recruiter default to team leaders/admins; do not echo the password in a toast
Normalise phone numbers (digits only / last 10) for duplicate detection in create_lead and check-duplicate; also run the duplicate check on debounce-while-typing, not just onBlur
Split server.py (1589 lines) into routers (auth/leads/calls/dashboard/admin) and replace raw dict bodies with Pydantic models on PATCH/POST endpoints
critical_code_review_comments: App.js wraps every page in <Protected> only (auth check) — there is no authorisation layer, so all admin screens are reachable by URL for any logged-in user.
server.py action_required() mixes scoped lead queries with unscoped db.interviews.find({}) / db.joinings.find(...) / all-recruiter call counts — the scope leak is inside one endpoint, easy to miss.

Frontend mutation handlers rely on api interceptors for errors but there is no interceptor toast; every await api.post/patch without .catch becomes an unhandled rejection (observed as pageerror on 403).
enrich_interview/enrich_joining perform 4 sequential find_one calls per row; batch with name maps like enrich_lead already does.
Recruiters.js resetPw hardcodes the password literal in the client; the password policy belongs on the server.

rca_of_the_issue: Role enforcement was implemented on write endpoints via require_role but not on read endpoints (/recruiters, leaderboard, parts of action-required) and not at all in the React router — <Protected> only checks for a token. Consequently the sidebar is the only thing hiding admin functionality, so any recruiter can read the full roster and cross-recruiter pipeline data by URL. Secondary root cause: frontend mutation handlers assume success (no .catch), so when the backend does correctly return 403 (e.g. PATCH /settings from a recruiter) the user sees no feedback and the failure only shows up as an unhandled promise rejection in the console.
